A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same DiTF study, including the equations, tables, figures and appendices. Relocated limitations and renumbered references can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original DiTF correspondence and segmentation experiments, activation analyses, ablations and supplementary evaluations in Appendices C-E.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and analyses, including the benchmark outcomes in Tables 2-6 and 8-9.

M1.justification: Sections 3-4 and Appendix C retain the same AdaLN modulation, channel discard, and optional DINOv2/PCA feature integration. Describing DiTF explicitly as 'AdaLN-based' does not change its procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate semantic correspondence on SPair-71k, PF-Pascal and the three AP-10K subsets, geometric correspondence on HPatches, temporal correspondence on DAVIS-2017, and semantic segmentation on ADE20K.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 2-3, 6, 8 and 9 and the qualitative comparisons. Newly cited TinyFusion and ViDiT-Q are discussed as related work, not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: The evaluation metrics, per-point versus per-image PCK conventions, model configurations, input resolutions, block/timestep choices and supplementary testing procedures remain unchanged in Section 5 and Appendices C-E.

E4.justification: Both retain the activation diagnostics, AdaLN/channel-discard and conditioning ablations, block/timestep sensitivity analysis, and qualitative correspondence examples. Tables 4-5, Figures 6 and 12, and the supplementary visualizations contain the same analyses.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains the same across-patch activation mean/variance summaries. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for benchmark performance.

E6.justification: Numerical entries, plotted results and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, DiTFflux retains 67.1% SPair-71k PCK@0.10 per point in Table 2 and 72.2 DAVIS J&F in Table 9.

T1.justification: The massive-activation definition and Equations (1)-(14) are unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theoretical results, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 removes the contribution statement claiming to be the first to identify and characterize massive activations in DiTs. It foregrounds the AdaLN connection already analyzed in v1, while retaining the training-free method and performance claims.

C2.justification: v1 Appendix G proposes lightweight fine-tuning to further adapt DiTs for representation learning; v2 omits this direction. The limitation concerning unexplored generative behavior is retained and reworded in Section 7. Existing experimental interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains the same implementation information, including model configurations, input resolutions, feature-layer choices and 1280-dimensional PCA. No code/data access information or other reproducibility details are added.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds TinyFusion and ViDiT-Q, acknowledging prior observations of DiT activation outliers affecting distillation and quantization. This limited positioning revision accompanies removal of the first-identification claim; the remaining cited works are retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contributions and conclusion receive limited rewrites. Limitations move from Appendix G to Section 7, and acknowledgments and contact metadata are added. Affiliation renumbering introduces a mismatch: Hong Kong is labeled 2 although its authors are marked 3.

P2.justification: All 19 figures and nine tables are retained without substantive redesign. The expanded title block changes first-page composition, and equation spacing and appendix table/text spacing are adjusted.

improvement.justification: The decisive gain is more careful attribution: v2 acknowledges existing DiT-outlier studies in Section 2 and removes the broad first-identification claim from its contributions. Methods and empirical support remain intact. The omitted fine-tuning suggestion and minor affiliation-label error are small drawbacks, outweighed by this limited improvement in research positioning.
